# $R_n=\star2$ and $Qo_n=\star3$ for every odd $n\ge 11$ (whole-board game)

**Summary**
1. Theorem: in the whole-board game on $C_n$ (race rule "count", e.p. on, an e.p.-capturable pawn is not passed, the game ends at the first passed pawn), for every odd $n\ge11$ the $(n+2)$-pawn positions $R_n=$ W5 B7 (W2 B4)$^{(n-9)/2}$ W2 W3B6 W3 W2B5 B5 W2 B4 and $Qo_n$ (W4 for W5) are $\star2$ resp. $\star3$ (meaning: H7); both fail at $n=9$ (LLLL).
2. The proof is the insertion proof of Section S13 (Lemmas 1-3 there, with the repaired "pattern file" and the written-out Lemma 3 of Note 1 of Section S15, §2b), at ONE fixed cut $c=6$ and ONE base $n_0=19$ for both families. The wall (files $2..n-7$) has odd length $n-8$ and W2 at both ends; neither end enters the lemmas (H1, H3).
3. C1: the reduced games at $n_0=19$ have 429 ($R$) and 1287 ($Qo$) nodes, no e.p. flag, no passed pawn, zone $\{n-7..n-3,n-1\}$ (for $Qo$ also $\{0,1\}$), signature NNPN resp. NNNP; files $2..11$ are exact pattern files in every node, and $R_{n+2}=\mathrm{ins}_6(R_n)$ was verified for $19\to21,\dots,57\to59$ (A) and, by independent programs, for $19\to21,\dots,31\to33$. C2: $n=11,13,15,17$ by direct search. E.p. convention: a flag is recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square (section 1).
4. Status: PROVED for odd $n\ge19$ given Lemmas 1-3 of Section S13, 2b and C1; CHECKED-2 for $n=11..17$ (finite checks by 5-6 programs each, section 7).

**How this note was checked.** The finite parts were computed by six independently written programs (section 0): A, the C program of Section S13, gave the reduced graphs, the pump and the unreduced searches; B rebuilt the reduced graphs on the project's game library `cylcgt`; C, D, E and O, Python engines written from the rules, rebuilt the reduced graphs, ran the pump steps and the unreduced searches, and tested Lemmas 2 and 3 on the actual nodes and on random positions; D and O were also tested against `cylcgt`'s rules. The hand proof was first checked by AI models of the same model family as the model that wrote it: two adversarial reviewers, one for the logic (which re-derived by hand every point where the odd configuration differs from the even cases) and one for the computations, found no mathematical defect; the corrections they asked for (wording, the e.p. convention, labels) are incorporated in the text. A model of another vendor then refereed the note and found the proof sound for the family as defined here; its own whole-board solver gave the two signatures for every odd $n=11..23$, and its own reduced graphs at $n=19$ have the node counts of C1. No human referee has checked it yet.

**Scope.** Proved: the whole-board game, race rule "count", e.p. flags recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square (game-equivalent to `pawns.py`'s raw flags, section 1), odd $n\ge11$, and equivalence to $\star2$ resp. $\star3$ against nim-heaps (H7). Not claimed: the component-sum model of `cylcgt`, the race rules "mover" and "opponent", even $n$ (Notes 1 and 2 of Section S15), or equivalence against arbitrary addends rather than nim-heaps. The hand part for the odd case was refereed by one model of another vendor (see above). $n=9$ is false.

## 1. Setting
Model, classes T/L/P/K, reduced game: as in Section S13 and in section 1 of Note 1 of Section S15 (race rule "count"). **E.p. convention** (as in Section S13, Model): an e.p. flag is recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square of the double step; a flag nobody could use is dropped. "No flag" in C1, H4, H6 and Lemmas 2-3 means this canonical convention. A, C, D, E, O use it, and B applies it through `difftest.norm_ep`; `cylcgt/pawns.py` itself records a flag after every double step, but its `ep_capturable` and `moves` act on a flag only when an enemy pawn stands beside the square, so an inert flag changes nothing but the name of the position. This was checked: with raw flags the reduced graphs have 434 ($R$) and 1302 ($Qo$) nodes for every odd $n=11..25$ (5 resp. 15 nodes carry an inert flag; 231 and 639 at $n=9$), and dropping the inert flags gives exactly the canonical graph, edge for edge, with the same signature (O; also a separate rebuild directly on `pawns.moves/passed/_child` at $n=19$: 434 nodes, 5 inert flags, node and edge sets equal to the canonical ones, 1100 raw vs 1082 canonical edges; likewise 1302, 15, 3886 vs 3827 for $Qo_{19}$).

Files $0..n-1$, $n$ odd $\ge11$: file 0 W5 ($R$) or W4 ($Qo$); file 1 B7; file $j$ ($2\le j\le n-7$) W2 if $j$ is even, B4 if $j$ is odd; then W3B6 ($n-6$), W3 ($n-5$), W2B5 ($n-4$), B5 ($n-3$), W2 ($n-2$), B4 ($n-1$).
That is $2+(n-8)+8=n+2$ pawns. The **wall** is files $2..n-7$: type E (black pawn two ranks above the white one), length $n-8$ (odd), W2 on file 2 (beside B7) and on file $n-7$ (beside W3B6). **Pattern file** (Note 1 of Section S15, section 2): a wall file whose content is exactly its start pawn. $\mathrm{ins}_c$ as in Lemma 3. $R_n$ ($Qo_n$) also denotes the reduced game, $\mathrm{start}_n$ its root. $Z_n=\{n-7,\dots,n-3,n-1\}$ ($R$), $\{0,1\}\cup\{n-7,\dots,n-3,n-1\}$ ($Qo$).

Lemma 1: a side wins $G+\star h$ moving first iff it wins the reduced game moving first. Lemma 2: for a wall pawn $q$ of the player $Z$ to move with pattern neighbour files, (a) $Z$ has no passed pawn after any move of $q$, (b) if $c$ has no flag and the window $j-1..j+3$ (or $j-3..j+1$) consists of pattern files, every move of $q$ is L or P. Lemma 3: if $p$ has no passer, no flag, and files $c-4..c+5$ are pattern files, then the K-children and the existence of T-moves of $\mathrm{ins}_c(p)$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_c$-images of those of $p$.

## 2. The cut and the base
Zone and pattern files. By C1, in every node of the reduced game of $G_n$ ($n\ge19$) all files outside $Z_n$ keep their start content. So files $2..n-8$ are pattern files of every node. The arc $A=\{c-4..c+5\}$ lies in $[2,n-8]$ iff $6\le c\le n-13$; the least $n$ is $n_0=19$, where $c=6$ is the only cut (`pump_verify.py` finds $c=6$ automatically at $19\to21$), and $c=6$ is admissible for every $n\ge19$. $A=\{2..11\}$ never wraps: the outside $12..n-1,0,1$ is one cyclic arc, which contains $Z_n$ and the files 0, 1 (not touched by $\mathrm{ins}_6$). $\mathrm{ins}_6$ fixes files $0..6$ and shifts files $\ge7$ by 2, so $\mathrm{ins}_6(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$. The range $6\le c\le n-13$ is what Lemma 3's arc hypothesis needs, so it is sufficient, not necessary: the computation shows that $\mathrm{ins}_c:G_n\to G_{n+2}$ is an isomorphism of the reduced graphs for every $c=2..n-9$ (O, $n=19..31$), and for $n=11..17$ at some cuts (only $c=2$ at $n=11$; $c=2..8$ at $n=17$). So the graphs for $n<19$ are also $\mathrm{ins}$-images of each other, but they do not satisfy Lemma 3's hypothesis (no ten-file arc of unchanged wall files) and are covered by C2, not by the induction.

## 3. Hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3
**H1 (wall, phase, ends).** The wall alternates W2 (even) / B4 (odd). $\mathrm{ins}_6$ inserts copies of file 7 (B4) and file 6 (W2) after file 6, so the new files 7, 8 continue the phase; $\mathrm{ins}_6(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ for $n\ge14$ (files 6, 7 are wall files), which covers $n\ge19$. The phase and ends differ from $E_n$ (Section S13), $P_n$ and $Q_n$ (Notes 1 and 2) (here W2 at both ends), but Lemma 2(b) uses only the cases W2$\to$3, W2$\to$4 (e.p.) and B4$\to$3 of the proof of Lemma 2(b) in Section S13, and Lemma 3 only the views of pawns (Note 1 of Section S15, H2 and 2b); neither uses a file's parity or a wall end.

**H2 (no capture by $q$).** With pattern neighbours the capture squares of $q$ on rank 3 are empty, and B4 cannot take e.p. a W2 that has not moved (Note 1 of Section S15, H3).

**H3 (windows at the two ends of the arc).** Central pawns: files $c-3..c+4=3..10$ of $p$, and $3..12$ of $\hat p=\mathrm{ins}_6(p)$ (arc $2..13$). Window of $q$ on file $j$: $j-1..j+3$ if $j\le c+2$ (resp. $c+4$ in $\hat p$), else $j-3..j+1$; all lie in the arc. *Left end:* $j=3$, $q=$B4, window $2..6$ (file 2 is the first wall file, W2 beside B7 on file 1; files 0, 1 are in no window): after B4$\to$3 the W2 on file 4 takes on $(3,3)$ and is passed (files $2,3,4$ then hold no black pawn), the black B4 on file 5 stays blocked by W2 on file 6. *Right end:* $j=10$ in $p$ ($j=12$ in $\hat p$), $q=$W2, window $7..11$ ($9..13$): after W2$\to$3, resp. $\to$4, B4 on $j-1$ takes (e.p. after $\to$4); the W2 on $j-2$ stays blocked by B4 on $j-3$. The window ends at file $11=n_0-8$ (resp. 13), so the wall-end file $n-7$ (W2, inside $Z_n$) is never part of a window. In 18 of 429 ($R$), 54 of 1287 ($Qo$) nodes the double step of $q$ on file 10 is L, not P: the W2 on file 12 has left, so B4 on file 11 is passed, the "$Y$ has a passer" branch of Lemma 2(b); the proof needs only that central moves are neither T nor K, so nothing breaks (as in Note 1 of Section S15, H2, end case).

**H4 (start).** $\mathrm{start}_n$ has no passed pawn and no flag: W5/W4 (0) is blocked by B7 (1), B7 by W5/W4; a wall W2 by the B4 on an adjacent file (file 2: B4 on 3; file $n-7$: B4 on $n-8$), a wall B4 on file $j$ by W2 on $j-1$; W3B6 (file $n-6$): each blocks the other; W3 ($n-5$) by B6; W2B5 ($n-4$): each blocks the other; B5 ($n-3$) by W2 ($n-4$); W2 ($n-2$) by B5; B4 ($n-1$) by W2 ($n-2$). E ran the passed-pawn test on all nodes: none has a passer.

**H5 (race rule).** Lemma 2 never uses the race; in Lemma 3 the passed pawns of $c_\mu$ and $\mathrm{ins}_6(c_\mu)$ coincide (V3), so any rule that depends on the passed pawns and on who moved gives the same class (Note 1 of Section S15, H4). The value is rule-specific, the lemmas are not.

**H6 (invariant).** $I_n$: no node of the reduced game has a flag, and every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_n$ outside $Z_n$. $I_{19}$ is C1. If $I_n$ holds ($n\ge19$): every node is non-terminal with no flag, and $A$ consists of pattern files (section 2), so Lemma 3 applies to every node with $c=6$; with H4 and induction on the distance from the root, nodes, K-edges and T-flags of $R_{n+2}$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_6$-images of those of $R_n$. An image has no flag; it agrees with $\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ outside $Z_{n+2}$ since files 7, 8 are copies of pattern files 7, 6 and $\mathrm{ins}_6(Z_n)=Z_{n+2}$. So $I_{n+2}$.

**H7 (meaning of $=\star k$; heaps).** As in Section S13 and in H8 of Note 1 of Section S15: $G=\star k$ means that for every heap $\star h$, $h<256$ (a passed pawn is worth $\pm256$), $G+\star h$ and $\star k+\star h$ have the same outcome, namely P for $h=k$ and N otherwise. It is the whole-board/heap-sum convention, not $G+X\equiv\star k+X$ for every game $X$. *R, $k=2$:* the signature of $R_n+\star h$ is N, N, P for $h=0,1,2$ (C1R); for every $h\ge3$, $R_n+\star h$ has the heap move to the P-position $R_n+\star2$, so it is N. *Qo, $k=3$:* N, N, N, P for $h=0..3$; for $h\ge4$ the move to $Qo_n+\star3$ gives N. The start has no flag and neither do the reduced nodes, so the e.p. convention across a heap move is immaterial (E ran both readings "keep" and "expire": identical results).

## 4. Finite checks
**C1R, C1Q ($n_0=19$).** A (`pump_verify.py R 19 59` with the cut fixed at 6, same for Qo): $n=19$ has 429 nodes, 805 K-, 653 T-moves, zone $\{12,13,14,15,16,18\}$, ep=0, NNPNNNNN ($h\le7$), resp. 1287, 2996, 1959, zone $\{0,1,12..16,18\}$, NNNPNNNN. B: the `cylcgt` rebuild equals A's graph (nodes and $(\text{src},\text{side},\text{target})$ triples: 1082 = 805 + 277, resp. 3827 = 2996 + 831) for $n=11..21$, $n=19$ included. E (`odd/check_odd.py`): the same counts, zone, no flag, signature NNPNN / NNNPN ($h\le4$), no passed pawn of either colour in any node, and files $2..11$ (and $2..13$ at $n=21$, $2..15$ at $n=23$) equal to the exact pattern W2 (even), B4 (odd) in every node. C, D, O (section 7) rebuilt both graphs from the rules: the same counts, zone, no flag, no passed pawn of either colour in any node, files $2..n-8$ exact pattern in every node, signatures NNPN / NNNP, for every odd $n=11..25$ (D: $n=11..19$ and $R_{21}$; C: $n\le21$). A rerun of D's and O's builds at $n=19$ (both families) gave the same numbers.

**Pump (S1).** A: for $n=19,21,\dots,59$ both families keep 429 / 1287 nodes, zone $Z_n$, ep=0, the signature; each of the 20 steps $19\to21,\dots,57\to59$ with the fixed cut $c=6$ reports "start->start True, nodes onto True, kept+T edges equal True". E: $\mathrm{ins}_6(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$, $R_{n+2}=\mathrm{ins}_6(R_n)$ node for node with equal K- and T-children for $n=19,21$ (858 resp. 2574 (node, side) pairs per step). D (cut $c=6$): $R$ for $19\to21\to23\to25\to27$, $Qo$ for $19\to21\to23\to25$, all "start->start, nodes onto, K-edges and T-flags equal"; O: both families for $19\to21\to\dots\to33$; a rerun of D's $R$ step $19\to21$ at $c=6$ gave True. The graphs of O, E, C are identical node for node and edge for edge for $n=9..25$ (C for $n\le21$) and equal every number in A's pump output for $n=11..59$; D's graphs agree with them in every count (nodes, K, T, flags, passers), zone and signature for $n=11..19$ (and $R_{21}$).

**Lemmas 2, 3 on the actual nodes (S3, E).** Lemma 2 on every central wall pawn (files $3..10$ at $n=19$, $3..12$ at $n=21$), both colours, with the windows of H3: $R$: 3432 q-positions, 5148 moves at $n=19$ (4290, 6435 at $n=21$); $Qo$: 10296, 15444 ($n=19$), 12870, 19305 ($n=21$); (a) 0 failures, (b) 0 T or K moves, every move L or P (file 3 and the left end: all P; right end $j=c+4$: 18 L + 840 P for $R$, 54 L + 2520 P for $Qo$). Lemma 3 recomputed on every $\mathrm{ins}_6(p)$ (not via the explored graph): 0 mismatches. Control: for the cuts $c=7..10$ Lemma 3's conclusion still holds on the nodes of $n=19$ although the arc meets the zone (radius 5 is conservative), for $c=11$ (arc $7..16$) it fails at 48 of 858 ($R$) and 150 of 2574 ($Qo$) (node, side) pairs, so the test can fail. That control is weak (it only looks at reachable nodes). A stronger one is D's random test with arbitrary content outside the arc (`verify_logicOdd/t_random.py`): positions are the start with 1-4 files outside the arc $2..11$ replaced by random contents, or a node plus 1-2 arbitrary moves, kept if they have no passer and no flag; K-children and the T-flag of $p$ are compared with those of $\mathrm{ins}_6(p)$ (about 100k K-children compared in all, 0 mismatches: $R_{19}$ 4000, $Qo_{19}$ 4000, $R_{21}$ 2000, $Qo_{25}$ 1500, $R_{27}$ 1500 positions, plus 2500 + 2500 node-walk positions). Cutting at $c\ne6$ while the same outside content is randomized gives 0 mismatches at $c=5,7,9$ (the radius-5 hypothesis is conservative) and mismatches at $c=10$ (208 of 1500), $c=11$ (233) and $c=12$ (1311), so the test fails when the hypothesis fails (a rerun with other seeds: 0 mismatches at $c=6$ and $c=7$, 51 of 400 at $c=10$). Lemma 2 with garbage outside the five-file window (two runs of 30000 positions per family, every wall file, both window directions): 0 violations of (a) or (b). On the nodes, D compares every move of every non-central pawn with its $\mathrm{ins}_6$-image (class T/L/P/K): $R_{19}$ 7131 moves, $Qo_{19}$ 20964, 0 mismatches; 242 resp. 726 of these are races (both sides passed), including ties (1 resp. 3), and all agree. O recomputes Lemma 3 on every $\mathrm{ins}_6(p)$ at $n=19,21,23$ (858 resp. 2574 (node, side) pairs per $n$): 0 mismatches. D and O reproduce the Lemma 2 tallies above exactly, including the right-end double step (18 of 429 and 54 of 1287 nodes: L because $q$'s double step leaves B4 on file 11 passed once W2 on file 12 has moved), and O repeats Lemma 2 with every wall file $3..n-8$ having an exact-pattern window inside the files $2..n-7$ (0 failures).

**C2, C3 (base cases).** Direct search, no poison pruning: A (odd $n=9..59$: LLLL at 9, then 25 lines NNPN; nodes 2916, 3654, 4392, 5130 for $n=11,13,15,17$) and for $Qo$ (LLLL, then 25 lines NNNP; 7780, 9749, 11718, 13687). E (`odd/base_cases.py`), $h\le4$, "keep" and "expire": NNPNN ($R$) / NNNPN ($Qo$) for $n=11..21$ (4628, 5832, 7036, 8240 states for $R$, $n=11..17$; 12239, 15451, 18663, 21875 for $Qo$), LLLLL at $n=9$. Each job ran as one process; the Python jobs peaked at 27 MB (E) and 45 MB (A's pump).
*Further runs (section 7).* The same short-circuit search, $h\le6$, in O, E and C for every odd $n=9..25$: NNPNNNN ($R$, $n\ge11$) / NNNPNNN ($Qo$), LLLLLLL at $n=9$, with identical state counts and both e.p.-across-heap readings; in D for $n=9..19$, each time also against the signature of the reduced graph, which is a second, different route to C2 (Lemma 1). Searches that evaluate every child and every heap move (no early exit, $h\le4$): $R_9$ and $Qo_9$ LLLLL (D, O); $R_{11}$ NNPNN (D: 885,125 states, O: 885,125 keep / 836,505 expire; the two engines give the same state count); $Qo_{11}$ NNNPN (O: 1,662,552 / 1,567,783 states); $R_{13}$ NNPNN (O, keep only: 4,261,697 states). Not run without early exit: $R_{15}$, $R_{17}$, $Qo_{13}$, $Qo_{15}$, $Qo_{17}$ (memory), so for these the short-circuit solvers (A, C, D, E, O, which agree) and the reduced-graph solution carry C2. O also gives $R_n=\star2$, $Qo_n=\star3$ ($h\le5$) for odd $n=27..41$, which is not used.

## 5. Proof of the Theorem
Let $n\ge19$ be odd. $I_{19}$ is C1; H6 gives $I_n$ for all odd $n\ge19$ and $R_n\cong R_{19}$, $Qo_n\cong Qo_{19}$ (nodes, K-edges, T-flags). By C1 and Lemma 1, $R_n+\star2$ and $Qo_n+\star3$ are P-positions, and the signatures are NNP.. resp. NNNP.. as in C1; H7 gives all heaps: $R_n=\star2$, $Qo_n=\star3$. For $n=11,13,15,17$ use C2 and H7 (the same heap step). $\blacksquare$ (T19: PROVED given L1-L3, C1; T: with C2.)

## 6. Gaps and caveats
1. **No gap found in the hypotheses.** What is new relative to Notes 1 and 2 of Section S15 is only the wall's phase and ends (W2 at both ends, odd length), the cut $c=6$ at the left end of the pattern run (the window of the pawn on file 3 starts at the first wall file 2, beside B7) and $n_0=19$; H1-H3 treat each. The one point to look at is the window of the pawn on file 3: it needs only that file 2 is a pattern file, which holds in every node (file 2 is outside $Z_n$ and its W2 never moves in the reduced game: its 2 moves per node are P in all nodes, C1 information). Every point where the odd configuration differs from the even cases (left end $j=3$ with window $2..6$, right end $j=10$ in $p$ and $j=12$ in $\hat p$ with the e.p. double step, odd wall length, W2 at both ends, the zones touching the arc, e.p. and race handling) was re-derived by hand in the logic check, with no step changed; the computational check recomputed the facts these arguments cite (zones, windows, tallies, pump).
2. **Lemmas 1-3 are cited, not re-proved**; their hand proofs are those of Section S13 and 2b, refereed as sound for $P_n$ and $Q_n$ (Notes 1 and 2 of Section S15). The truth of Lemma 2(b) itself rests on Section S13 and on the referees of Notes 1 and 2.
3. **C1, C2 are computer facts**: the theorem for $n\ge19$ is "proved modulo C1", the theorem for $n=11..17$ is a finite computation. A, C, D, E, O were written from one rule description (B uses the project's `pawns.py`); a shared misreading is excluded only by differential tests against `pawns.py`: D on $R_{19}$, $Qo_{19}$ (7463 positions, 222,556 child records), O on 64,886 positions with 755,453 moves (including e.p. positions and both-sides-passed races), E in Note 1 of Section S15 (about 61k positions): 0 differences everywhere (D and O together: 72k positions, about 980k child records). The searches for $n=11..17$ are short-circuit solvers; the no-early-exit solver was run for $R_9$, $Qo_9$, $R_{11}$, $Qo_{11}$ and $R_{13}$ ($h\le4$) only, not for $R_{15}$, $R_{17}$, $Qo_{13}$, $Qo_{15}$, $Qo_{17}$ (section 4); for these the short-circuit solvers (five programs) and the solution of the reduced graph (a different route, via Lemma 1) agree. Wherever a no-early-exit run exists it agrees with the short-circuit result, at $n=9$ as well.
4. **Scope**: whole-board game, race rule "count", e.p. flags recorded only if an enemy pawn stands beside the landing square (game-equivalent to `pawns.py`'s raw flags, section 1); race-rule sensitivity and the component-sum model were not examined for the odd families; $R_9$, $Qo_9$ are not $\star2$, $\star3$ (C3).
5. The graphs already have 429 / 1287 nodes at $n=11..17$ (zones as in A's pump output), but $n<19$ has no ten-file arc of unchanged wall files, so those $n$ are not instances of the induction and rest on C2. $n=9$ is not an instance of the pump either: its reduced graphs are different (2082 nodes for $R$ with files $0$ and $8$ in the zone, 5276 for $Qo$) and have signature LLLL, as C3 says.
6. The sensitivity control on the nodes (Lemma 3 fails only at $c=11$) is weak; the random-outside control of section 4 is the one to cite.

## 7. Further checks
**By program D** (independent of A, B, E). C1: $R_{19}$ 429 nodes, 805 K, 653 T; $Qo_{19}$ 1287, 2996, 1959; no flagged node, no passer in any node, zones $\{12..16,18\}$ and $\{0,1,12..16,18\}$, files $2..11$ exact pattern in every node, signatures NNPN / NNNP; the same at $R_{21}$ and at $n=11..17$ ($R$) and $n=11,13$ ($Qo$). Pump at $c=6$: $R$ for $19\to21,\dots,25\to27$, $Qo$ for $19\to21,\dots,23\to25$, all true. Differential test against `cylcgt/pawns.py` (moves, passed pawns, terminal verdict with the count race): $R_{19}$ 4209 positions, 127,244 child records; $Qo_{19}$ 3254 positions, 95,312 child records; 0 mismatches. Random stress tests of Lemma 3 with arbitrary content outside the arc (about 100k K-children, 0 mismatches) and of Lemma 2 with garbage outside the window (two runs of 30000 positions per family, 0 violations); the control fails at $c=10,11,12$ and passes at $c=5,7,9$. Lemma 2 (a), (b) on every central wall pawn of every node at $n=19,21$ (the tallies of section 4, including the 18 / 54 L double steps at the right end, traced to B4 on file 11 becoming passed); every far-pawn move compared with its $\mathrm{ins}_6$-image, including 242 / 726 races with ties. Unreduced search $R_n$, $Qo_n$, $n=9..19$, both e.p. readings, against the reduced-graph solution; no-early-exit for $R_9$, $R_{11}$, $Qo_9$. The left end ($j=3$, window $2..6$), the right end ($j=10$ in $p$, $j=12$ in $\hat p$) and the arc/zone arithmetic were re-derived by hand and found as stated in H1-H3.

**By program O** (written from the rules, standard library only; with E and C under their own drivers; none of A's `rg.c`, `cylcgt`'s game-value code, `check_odd.py` or `base_cases.py` was used). (a) $G+\star h$, $h=0..6$, odd $n=9..25$ in O, E, C: LLLLLLL at $n=9$, NNPNNNN ($R$) / NNNPNNN ($Qo$) for every odd $n=11..25$, identical state counts, both e.p.-across-heap readings and raw flags; $h\le5$ for odd $n=27..41$ in O. No-early-exit: $R_9$, $Qo_9$, $R_{11}$, $Qo_{11}$ (both readings, $h\le4$) and $R_{13}$ (keep). (b) Reduced graphs for odd $n=9..25$: 429 / 805 / 653 and 1287 / 2996 / 1959 for every $n\ge11$, 277 and 831 (node, side) pairs with a T-move, node for node and edge for edge identical to E ($n=9..25$) and C ($n=9..21$), every number equal to A's pump output; at $n=9$ the graphs are different (2082, 5276 nodes) and the signature is LLLL. (c) $\mathrm{ins}_6$: start to start and nodes onto nodes with K- and T-children preserved for $19\to21,\dots,31\to33$ in both families; Lemma 3 recomputed on every $\mathrm{ins}_6(p)$ at $n=19,21,23$: 0 mismatches; Lemma 2 tallies equal to those of section 4; control: 0 failures at $c=7..10$, 48 of 858 ($R$) and 150 of 2574 ($Qo$) at $c=11$. The isomorphism holds for every cut $c=2..n-9$. Raw e.p. flags: 434 / 1302 nodes, game-equivalent to the canonical graphs. Differential test of O against E, C and `pawns.py` (rules only): 64,886 positions (seeds 1, 7), 755,453 moves, 0 differences in moves, passed pawns, promotion distance or verdict.

**Spot reruns.** D rebuilt $R_{19}$ (429 / 805 / 653, zone $\{12..16,18\}$, NNPNN) and $Qo_{19}$ (1287 / 2996 / 1959, zone $\{0,1,12..16,18\}$, NNNPN); O at $n=19$ for both families gave the same numbers, NNPNNNNN / NNNPNNNN, E and C graph-identical, 434 / 1302 raw-flag nodes equivalent to the canonical ones. The raw-flag graph rebuilt directly on `pawns.moves/passed/_child` (a flag after every double step): $R_{19}$ 434 nodes, 5 with a flag, none live (an enemy pawn beside the landing square), 1100 edges; $Qo_{19}$ 1302, 15, 3886; after dropping inert flags the node and edge sets equal the canonical ones (1082, 3827 edges) in both. In `pawns.py`, `moves` sets a flag after every double step, `ep_capturable` and the e.p. capture act only if an enemy pawn stands beside the square, and Section S13 (Model) says a flag is recorded only in that case, which is the convention stated in section 1. D's tests with new seeds: Lemma 3 at $c=6$ on 400 random positions, 0 mismatches; the same test cut at $c=7$: 0, at $c=10$: 51 of 400 mismatches; Lemma 2 with garbage outside the window, $Qo_{19}$, 2000 positions: every move L or P; D's pump $R$ $19\to21$ at $c=6$: true. The numbers this note cites were checked against the program outputs they come from. `verify_logicOdd/engineD.py` is byte-identical to `verify_logic/engine.py`, and `oddeng.py` imports only the standard library.
